rationale: The source gives the same proper-filter axioms on a set, including omission of the empty set and upward/intersection closure. Definition only.
The source gives the standard base/FIP data used to generate a filter; the item repackages it as a three-clause downward-directed base with the library properness convention. Definition only.
The sources identify the upward closure of base data as the generated filter. The item adds the smallest-filter and idempotence clauses and expands the standard verification.
The source defines the finite-intersection property, while the item makes the empty-list convention and indexed-list formulation explicit. Definition only.
The standard FIP-to-filter construction and converse are sourced; the item combines them into an equivalence and expands the finite-induction and boundary cases.
The source defines an ultrafilter as a maximal proper filter under inclusion, exactly the item convention. Definition only.
The source records that the union of comparable filters is a filter. The item states the nonempty-chain form needed by Zorn and separately records the empty-chain upper bound.
The sources state that every proper filter/FIP family extends to an ultrafilter. The local proof is the standard Zorn argument expanded with the empty-chain case.
The source gives the equivalent maximality and complement-decision characterisations. The item supplies a fully expanded generated-filter proof.
The source identifies ultrafilters with prime filters and gives the complement decision law. The item derives binary and finite-union primeness, including n=0.
The sources place the ultrafilter lemma at the Boolean-prime-ideal strength and strictly below full AC relative to ZF consistency. The item is a library-specific implication/independence ledger.

The false claim reverses the sourced existence of free ultrafilters. The tail-filter witness and numbered refutation are locally written, with the ultrafilter lemma supplying the nonprincipal extension.
The standard principal-filter construction is sourced; the item specializes it to a nonempty generator C and proves the ultrafilter-if-and-only-if-singleton criterion.
The source gives exactly the principal ultrafilter at x as all subsets containing x. The item verifies it using the local generator and complement criteria.

The sources give the cofinite/Fréchet filter and its behavior on infinite sets. The item identifies it with the tail-generated filter on N and supplies an explicit parity witness showing it is not ultra.

The source states that a free ultrafilter on an infinite set is equivalently one containing the Fréchet filter and that such extensions exist via the ultrafilter lemma. The item expands the singleton exclusion.
The result is the finite-partition form of sourced finite primeness and complement exclusivity. The item states uniqueness and the n=0 boundary explicitly.
The counterclaim is recoverable from the standard filter axioms and principal-ultrafilter construction. The exact two-point witness and its verification are locally written.
The counterclaim is recoverable from the standard maximality/complement characterisation. The exact two-point intersection witness is locally chosen and checked.
The item is a convention warning derived from the sourced proper-filter definition: admitting the empty set produces the greatest weak filter P(X). The explicit verification is locally written.
The source defines well-orders by the least-element property and discusses the descending-sequence distinction without dependent choice, matching the item. Definition only.
The source gives order isomorphism as a bijection preserving the order in both directions, with the same well-order setting. Definition only.
The sources give initial segments of well-orders and the point-cut form. The item consolidates downward closure, proper segments, uniqueness, and intersection closure. Definition only.
The sources state transfinite induction on well-orders. The item uses the standard least-counterexample proof and explicitly notes its ZF/no-choice boundary.
The sources prove transfinite recursion; the item formulates the general well-order/class-function schema and expands the compatible-attempt construction with its Replacement uses.
Rigidity and uniqueness of well-order isomorphisms are standard consequences in the source development. The item packages four consequences and expands the least-moved-point proof.
The source gives the trichotomy/comparability theorem for well-orders. The local proof expands the canonical matching of isomorphic initial segments.
The sources define von Neumann ordinals as transitive sets well ordered by membership, exactly the item convention. Definition only.
The sources establish the standard membership, transitivity, union, intersection, and successor facts. The item combines these into one multi-clause lemma with explicit set-existence boundaries.
The sources state ordinal trichotomy and well-ordering by membership. The local proof derives it from well-order comparability and handles minima of nonempty ordinal families.
The proper-class result for all ordinals is standard in the sources. The item gives the usual self-membership contradiction in the local vocabulary.

The formal source proves Mostowski collapse and the set-theory notes identify well-order order types. The item specializes collapse to a well-order and expands existence, ordinal range, uniqueness, and the Foundation caveat.
The source uses the standard nonzero, nonsuccessor definition of a limit ordinal and the equivalent closure under successors. Definition only.
The source development identifies omega as the least infinite/limit ordinal and its members as finite ordinals. The item reconstructs this from the library natural-number axioms.
The sources state Hartogs theorem and its construction from well-orders of subsets. The local proof expands sethood, ordinal closure, leastness, and the no-injection argument.
The sources state and prove AC implies every set is well-orderable. The item uses the standard Zorn poset of well-ordered subsets ordered by end extension.
The sources give the converse by well-ordering the union and taking least elements. The local proof expands the graph construction and uniqueness.
The sources state the equivalence of AC and well-ordering; the item also folds in the already-published Zorn equivalence. The proof is a local implication ledger.

The sources define cardinals as initial ordinals and cardinal assignment by least equinumerous ordinal when well-orderability is available. The item makes its global AC convention and Hartogs set-bounding explicit. Definition only.
The remark compiles standard equivalences, weaker choice principles, and independence results into a library-specific ledger, with the external model claims delegated to the cited catalogue items.
The false claim negates the sourced Burali-Forti proper-class theorem. The refutation is the standard self-membership argument expanded through local ordinal facts.
The false claim deletes the sourced AC hypothesis from the well-ordering theorem. The local refutation chains the published equivalence with Cohen independence under the stated consistency condition.

The false claim conflates induction on a given well-order with choosing well-orders for arbitrary sets. The local refutation separates those established principles and identifies the actual ZF/AC boundary.
